notes:
I don't have any notes for you yet. My first attempt tried to load seven pages at once, and that went over the tool's usage limit. After that I had no tool calls left for this turn, so I couldn't read a single page.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for each point, and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. I won't write a commentary from memory and dress it up as sourced research.

**What I'll do next time**, reading the pages one at a time so I stay under the limit:

1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:**
   - Enduring Word: enduringword.com/bible-commentary/isaiah-18/
   - Bible Hub verse pages for 18:1–7 (Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary, Barnes, Gill and others), e.g. biblehub.com/commentaries/isaiah/18-1.htm
   - StudyLight (Gill's Exposition) for Isaiah 18
   - Precept Austin, if it has an Isaiah 18 page
2. **Differences between Protestant traditions:** Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Calvin's commentary on Isaiah (ccel.org), and searches on Ligonier, Grace to You, Desiring God and Got Questions. I'd look first at verse 7 (the nations bringing gifts to Zion: fulfilled in the past, in the church, or still to come) and at who the "people tall and smooth-skinned" in verse 2 are.
3. **Other views:**
   - The NET Bible notes (netbible.org) on the hard Hebrew words in verses 1–2 and on who is being addressed
   - Bible Odyssey on Cush and Isaiah's oracles against the nations
   - New Advent (the Church Fathers on Isaiah)

If you'd like, ask again and I'll start with Enduring Word and the Bible Hub pages, then work down the list.
